tagline: Ten miles at sea level across Old Tampa Bay.
intro: SR 60 leaves Clearwater and goes straight out across Old Tampa Bay on a low fill, palms and mangroves along it and a paved trail beside the road the whole way. About ten miles on it comes ashore at Rocky Point, a mile short of Tampa's airport.

Before it, the road between the two cities ran more than 30 miles around the top of the bay. Ben T. Davis, who owned a dredging company, began the fill in 1927 and worked at it whenever his dredges ran out of other jobs. It opened in 1934 with a 25-cent toll, then the longest over-water fill in the country. In 1948 the state renamed it for a member of the Road Board.

moments.title: Courtney Campbell Causeway
moments.text: Out in the bay the fill breaks for two elevated spans, and a public boat ramp sits on the north side just east of the largest.

moments.title: Ben T. Davis Beach
moments.text: At the east end the City of Tampa keeps a beach under the builder's name, which is where his name ended up.

moments.title: Rocky Point
moments.text: The Tampa landfall, home to Rocky Point Golf Course, one of Florida's oldest, and the world headquarters of Shriners International.
